items.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015
items.q: I picked out like Roberta Flack’s record and Bette Midler’s first record and there were some other things, and the Neville Brothers and then Freddie Hubbard and then this and that and this from Atlantic

ctx.x: I wanted to throw out a name that you know, Joel Dorn?

Yeah, he is one of the great ones. I sought him out. When I was about to do my first solo record for Atlantic in 1981 I gave some thought to it and I thought I’m just going to go through my collection and see who I like. And I picked out like Roberta Flack’s record and Bette Midler’s first record and there were some other things, and the Neville Brothers and then Freddie Hubbard and then this and that and this from Atlantic and I went I think Joel Dorn might be a good guy to talk to. So I made a cassette — that’s…
eclectic and that’s what he liked. And I had things by the Dixie Hummingbirds on there and I had vocalese and I had some pop things, and he liked that a lot.
